clue.text: Sequence featuring in advert for brewing equipment

indicators.note: a thing featuring in another appears within it, so the sequence word sits inside the advert word

parts.note: a teaser is an advert that gives little away to rouse curiosity
a train is a sequence, as in a train of events

explanation.surface: A commercial showing a series of shots of kit for making beer or tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea strainer catches the leaves when tea is poured, so it is a piece of kit for the brew.

clue.text: Learned soaring number in concert

indicators.note: soaring means rising, and in a down entry the learned word is read upwards

parts.note: got means learned, as in got the hang of it
ether is an anaesthetic, something that numbs, so a number

explanation.surface: An educated song that rises up in a live performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a song; read it as 'numb-er', a thing that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Working in concert means acting jointly, together.

clue.text: Workplaces had to be located with rest, oddly

parts.note: had, as in had dinner, means ate
to lie means to be situated, located

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of rest, first and third

explanation.surface: Workshops that had to be sited with a break, strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: Ateliers are artists' or designers' studios, places where creative work is done.

clue.text: Child joining a large comprehensive

parts.note: a tot is a small child
L is the clothing size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A child starting at a big comprehensive school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comprehensive' reads as a British state secondary school; it is the adjective meaning all-embracing.
explanation.definitionFit: Total and comprehensive both mean complete, covering everything.

clue.text: Tight flips in the middle of great move

indicators.note: the turned tight word goes in the middle of the great word

parts.note: ace means excellent, great

indicators.note: to flip is to turn over, so the tight word is read backwards

parts.note: taut means tight

explanation.surface: A drunk turns somersaults during a great dance move.
explanation.definitionFit: To actuate is to set in motion, to move a machine or person to act.

clue.text: Wings of nylon filled with a strong material

indicators.note: the two outside letters of nylon are filled with the a, which goes between them
wings are the sides, so only the first and last letters of nylon are used

parts.note: keen can mean strong, as in a keen wind or keen competition

explanation.surface: The edges of a nylon garment padded with a tough fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth, originally made in Nanjing, China.

clue.text: Terrace positioned externally ruined fancy entrance

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged
externally means on the outside, so only the outer letters of positioned are taken

explanation.surface: A terrace placed outside spoiled a grand doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'externally' takes P and D, the outside letters of 'positioned'; they join TERRACE as the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A red carpet is rolled out for a ceremonial arrival by VIPs, a lavish welcome.

clue.text: Sweet potatoes, peeled

indicators.note: peeling strips the skin, so the outer letters of the potatoes word are removed

parts.note: spuds is informal for potatoes

explanation.surface: Sweet potatoes, with their skins taken off, ready for cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet potatoes' reads as one vegetable; split them, and 'Sweet' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pud is British informal for pudding, a dessert course served after the main meal.

clue.text: Pair winning almost immediately

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the winning phrase loses its last letter

parts.note: on top means winning, ahead

explanation.surface: A couple winning almost at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronto is an informal borrowing from Italian meaning quickly, without delay, right now.

clue.text: Heroin stashed in dirty vessel

indicators.note: something stashed in another is hidden away inside it, so the drug letter goes inside

parts.note: dingy means grimy, dirty
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Drugs hidden aboard a grubby boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinghy is a small open boat, a type of vessel.

clue.text: Big jar picked up

indicators.note: something picked up is caught by the ear, signalling that a word is said aloud

parts.note: to jar is to grate, to have a harsh irritating effect

explanation.surface: A large pot that someone has lifted off the shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jar' looks like a noun for a pot, but it is the verb meaning to grate on the nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Great and big are ordinary synonyms describing large size.

clue.text: Muted, odd new pants acquired by fashionable people

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are taken on by the fashionable people word, so they follow it

parts.note: the ton is an old term for high society, the fashionable set

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, signalling the letters of odd new are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Odd new trousers gone quiet once picked up by the fashion crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'pants' means rubbish, so here it is the anagram signal, not trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something toned down has been made less loud or intense, so it is muted.

clue.text: Dodgy retail stores fight for free computer programmes

indicators.note: something that stores another holds it inside, so the fight word goes within the reworked letters
dodgy means unsound or unreliable, telling us the letters of retail are shuffled

parts.note: a war is a fight

explanation.surface: Shady shops that battle to give software away.
explanation.definitionFit: Trialware is software issued free for a limited trial period before purchase is required.

clue.text: A long intro from Hendrix?

parts.note: to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: A lengthy opening riff from Jimi Hendrix.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opening letter of the name Hendrix, spelt out as a word; the question mark flags that playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitch is the spelt-out name of the letter H, which begins the name Hendrix.

clue.text: Artist gatecrashes every exhibition, principally as a complaint

indicators.note: a gatecrasher pushes in uninvited, so the artist letters push inside the every word

parts.note: each means every
RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, so only the leading letter of exhibition is used

explanation.surface: A painter barges into every show, mainly to make a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' reads as a grievance; here it is an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Earache is a pain in the ear, and a complaint can mean a minor illness or ailment.

clue.text: Guy takes a drink in a stupor

parts.note: cat is jazz slang for a man, a guy
tonic is tonic water, a drink

explanation.surface: A man has a drink and ends up in a daze.
explanation.definitionFit: Catatonic describes a trance-like state of unresponsive immobility, a stupor.

clue.text: A lack of training? That's not gonna happen!

parts.note: no means none of, a lack of
PE is physical education, training at school

explanation.surface: Someone refuses outright to go without exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Nope is a casual, emphatic form of no, a flat refusal.

clue.text: Type of food in a tin, cooked without opening

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the reworked letters surround the opening word
cooked as in cooked the books, falsified, so the letters of a tin are shuffled

parts.note: a door is an opening

explanation.surface: A sort of meal in a can, heated up without being opened.
explanation.definitionFit: Tandoori food is Indian cooking roasted in a tandoor, a clay oven.

clue.text: Dissolute young trainee mostly overwhelmed with depression

indicators.note: the trainee word is overwhelmed, engulfed, by the depression word around it

parts.note: a dent is a hollow, a depression

indicators.note: mostly means most of, so the trainee word loses its last letter

parts.note: a cadet is a young trainee in the forces or police

explanation.surface: A debauched young recruit, largely swamped by gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' reads as gloom; it is a dent.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent and dissolute both describe self-indulgent moral decline and loose living.

clue.text: Boss of film company denied one Oscar

indicators.note: the film company word is denied, deprived of, the letters for one and Oscar

parts.note: a studio is a film-making company
I is the roman numeral one and O is Oscar in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A movie mogul refused a single Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a film mogul; it is the raised knob.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised knob or ornament, as is a stud on a belt or shield.

clue.text: Moderates needing restraint, being without power

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the restraint and being words go round the power letter

parts.note: a dam holds back water, a restraint
ens is a philosophical term for an entity or being
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Political centrists who need reining in, lacking any clout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderates' looks like a noun for centrists; it is a verb. 'without' means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: To dampen something is to lessen its force, so dampens means tones down or moderates.

clue.text: Fluster in the end a little bit and struggle to manage

indicators.note: only the final letter of fluster is taken

parts.note: a trace is a tiny amount

explanation.surface: Getting flustered at the last and battling to cope.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the exhausting competitive grind of working life, a constant scramble just to get by.

clue.text: Society function hosted by European leader for composer

indicators.note: the society and function letters are hosted by, held within, the leader word

parts.note: roi is French for king, a European leader
sin is the abbreviation for the sine function in trigonometry

explanation.surface: A society event put on by a continental head of state for a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian composer of operas such as The Barber of Seville.

clue.text: Provide compensation for bad TV

parts.note: off means gone bad, as with milk
a TV is a television set

explanation.surface: Someone seeking damages for poor television programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: To offset is to counterbalance, making up for a loss or cost.

clue.text: Trial a combination of having no booze and exercise

parts.note: dry means without alcohol, as in a dry month
a run is exercise

explanation.surface: An experiment combining abstinence from alcohol with workouts.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry run is a rehearsal or practice attempt before the real thing.

clue.text: Duke eclipsing king and cardinal

indicators.note: to eclipse is to cover over, so the duke word goes round the king letter

parts.note: dukes is slang for fists, so a duke is a fist
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A nobleman outshining both a monarch and a senior churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests a churchman; here it is the adjective meaning chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal as an adjective means of foremost importance, principal, as in a cardinal rule; first carries that same sense.

clue.text: Within minutes, idiot adviser rebuffed radio and the press etc

indicators.note: the idiot word sits within the two letters for minutes

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for minute, so MM gives minutes
an ass is a fool

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests being pushed back, so the adviser word is read backwards

parts.note: an aide is an assistant who advises

explanation.surface: In no time, a foolish consultant is turned away by broadcasters and newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: The mass media are the means of communication, such as broadcasting and newspapers, that reach large audiences.

clue.text: Wipe the floor with flash young boxer?

parts.note: mo is short for moment, as is a flash
a boxer is a breed of dog, and a young dog is a pup

explanation.surface: Thrash a flashy junior fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' is the dog breed, not a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop up is to deal with the last opposition decisively, as to thrash or wipe the floor with someone.

clue.text: Tranquil, mainly secure island location in Africa

indicators.note: mainly means for the most part, so the final letter of the tranquil word is dropped

parts.note: serene means calm, tranquil
to secure something is to get it
I is a map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A calm, largely safe island spot on the African continent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a vast plain and national park in Tanzania, famed for wildlife migrations.

clue.text: Familiar issue beginning to encumber investigation

parts.note: prob is a familiar, informal short form of problem, an issue

indicators.note: the beginning letter of encumber alone is taken

explanation.surface: A well-known matter starting to weigh down an inquiry.
explanation.definitionFit: A probe is a thorough inquiry, as into wrongdoing.

clue.text: Container of eggs nearly knocked over

indicators.note: knocked over means upended, so the shortened word is read backwards

parts.note: nits are the eggs of lice

explanation.walkthrough: The eggs are not hen's eggs but nits, the eggs of lice.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin is a metal can or box used to hold and store things.

clue.text: Pie contains nuts, for example

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, telling us the letters of pie contains are scrambled

explanation.surface: A pie filled with nuts, as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like the filling; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A case in point is an instance that illustrates the matter under discussion, an example.
